extracted.subtask_description: Contemporary newspaper reporting of World War II events, policies and proclamations (military actions, occupation measures, diplomatic statements, and government proclamations) intended for a general readership.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allied post-war punishment of war criminals
rubrics_metrics.description: Allied victory terms would call for punishment of 'ringleaders' responsible for organized murder and other atrocities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Announcement that proposed United Nations commission will investigate and fix guilt for crimes against civilian populations; Allied inter-allied committee of refugees had already prepared lists of those actively responsible for Axis terror in their homelands. The announcement was used as a propaganda weapon and broadcast in many languages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish enemy peoples from their warlords and Quislings
rubrics_metrics.description: Announcements of policy drew a clearer line between the enemy peoples themselves and their warlords and Quislings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This distinction was intended to blunt propaganda that defeat would mean collective punishment of Germans and to undercut collaborationist regimes; it also signaled that punishment would target leaders rather than entire populations and could reduce hopes for negotiated peace with collaborationists.

rubrics_metrics.name: German forced labor decree for Belgium and northern France
rubrics_metrics.description: Belgians may be compelled to undertake work of any kind in Belgium or in Reich territory according to their capabilities and their physical condition; compulsory for men between 18 and 50 and for unmarried women between 25 and 35; use of labor books introduced and every male between 18 and 50 must prove that he is employed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Free Belgian news agency noted the decree compared to measures recently invoked by the Vichy regime to draft labor for Germany’s war industry; believed that Belgian unemployed would be taken for work in Germany immediately.

rubrics_metrics.name: German method to 'Hitlerize' occupied countries (Denmark example)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reported German preparations to 'Hitlerize Denmark' in the very near future as a step to absorbing her in a 'federation of German countries' by abolishing the Danish Constitution, dissolving political parties and launching 'a regime of political terror'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scandinavian sources viewed this as a systematic replacement of native Nazis with German Nazis and absorption of conquered peoples into a German federation; critical dates (e.g., arrival/movement of Free Nazi Corps) could affect implementation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Geneva Convention Article II forbids fettering of prisoners
rubrics_metrics.description: The fettering/manacling of prisoners 'is expressly forbidden by Article II of the Geneva Convention (governing humane treatment of prisoners)'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: British Government cited this provision in condemning German chaining of Dieppe prisoners; the legal prohibition was invoked as the basis for demands and diplomatic/propaganda responses and to justify calls for impartial investigation.

rubrics_metrics.name: British retaliatory policy on POW shackling (counter-measure)
rubrics_metrics.description: The British War Office announced that unless the German government releases prisoners captured at Dieppe from their chains, an equal number of German prisoners of war will be manacled and chained as from noon Saturday.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Described as a counter-measure specifically against Axis prisoners now in British prison camps; officials stressed Britain would not countenance shackling of prisoners captured in the field and framed the step as reprisal unless Germans rescinded their order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Request for neutral impartial probe of POW treatment
rubrics_metrics.description: Suggestion to have the neutral Swiss make an impartial investigation of German allegations about treatment of prisoners.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: British noted Germans ignored the suggestion; principle emphasizes use of neutral third party to verify allegations about POW mistreatment rather than relying on partisan claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conditions for British negotiations with Gandhi/Congress
rubrics_metrics.description: Mohandas K. Gandhi’s Congress party must shun violence and drop any plan to win its aims through revolution before the British will negotiate with it; Britain refused negotiations 'so long as there were threats of trouble' and while Congress was not 'prepared to come to an agreed settlement with the rest of the country.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Government stated 'door remains open' for favorable consideration of proposals within the framework of the British declaration (promise of dominion status after the war); violence was explicitly cited as barring parley and as risking communal conflict.

rubrics_metrics.name: Church of England guidance on marriage ceremonies for Allied soldiers
rubrics_metrics.description: Diocesan chancellors of the Church of England recommended that no marriage ceremonies be performed for United States or Canadian soldiers who do not have the formal permission of their commanding officers, as required by army regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clergy were advised to follow army regulations; recommendation ties ecclesiastical practice to military discipline and permission procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: British restrictions on immigration to Northern Ireland
rubrics_metrics.description: All persons not resident there before January, 1940, would be required to obtain entry permits to Northern Ireland; other regulations in the interest of national security would permit the deportation of undesirables, issued only for six months.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measures were portrayed as temporary national-security regulations responding to increased political activity since arrival of American troops and significant immigration into Northern Ireland during the previous two years.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of multilingual broadcasting as propaganda of Allied policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Britain broadcast the full announcement of agreement with the United States on post-war punishment of war criminals in a score of languages to the peoples of Europe, Africa and Asia.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Framed as putting the agreement into action as a propaganda weapon to influence occupied and neutral populations, to publicize Allied intentions and to help distinguish between rulers and people.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establishment of United Nations commission to investigate war crimes
rubrics_metrics.description: Plans announced for a United Nations commission to fix the guilt of crimes against civilian populations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commission expected to build on prior inter-allied work (lists prepared by refugee committees) to identify those responsible for Axis terror; used both as legal/political instrument and as propaganda to occupied peoples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vichy/German internment list transparency (incomplete/revised lists)
rubrics_metrics.description: Vichy published an incomplete and unrevised list of Americans interned by the Germans at Vittel; the US Embassy emphasized the list did not include all those taken into custody and that some named might later have been released.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Highlights the importance of accurate, updated lists for diplomatic protection and public information; indicates limitations of host/occupying-power disclosures.
